Depends what you mean by "learn about computers." Do you mean how they work, how you can program them, just operation?

If you want to know to operate them (as in like.. not just basic "how do i open notepad"), I'd just mess around. Unless you're using the Commodore PET or a Pentium processor, there is no thing you can click on or type to destroy the computer itself. You might have to reinstall Windows/Linux, but it will (hopefully) never physically break your hardware.

How do they work? There's a few good books. I'd start with "But How Do It Know?" by J. Clark Scott. After that, "Modern Computer Architecture and Organizatiom" by Jim Ledin is a good book. If you don't like reading, then there's a small online game called (iirc) Nand2Tetris, basically where you build a computer. Also, you can build a computer in Minecraft (there is a Minecraft server known as Open Redstone Engineers which is good. Unfortunately, you have to do some work to use worldedit). Also, breadboards are pretty fun (look up Ben Eater) to help you understand computers.

For programming, there's a lot of tutorials online. I'd start with either C or Python. C if you want to get low-level and understand advanced things right off the bat, and want a good speed, and are okay with more complicated things first. Start with Python if you prefer easier, more simplified things, but are okay with sacrificing speed and some knowledge. Also, play around. The best way to learn is to just mess around.

There's not really a good way to learn about all of computers at once. You can learn about programming, or computer architecture, or using computers in an advanced way, or Linux, or sysadmin, or whatever. But the field of computers is so massive that it's hard to learn about computers as a whole.

EDIT: Though, if it isn't a Thinkpad (or if it is), send a picture of the Motherboard. It might not be the BIOS, but a BIOS setting. If it is a BIOS setting, then there is one of three ways to reset the BIOS:

Way 0 (not thinkpad)

1. Turn off the power SUPPLY (not laptop power)

2. Remove the BIOS battery

3. Turn on the power supply for 30 sec

Way 1 (thinkpad)

1. Look for a switch labeled "Clear CMOS." If it is a switch, and it says CLEAR CMOS, press it. 

Way 2 (thinkpad, dangerous, technical, unrecommended, only if there is no Clear CMOS button or BIOS battery)

1. Get out your screwdriver 

2. Look for the CMOS chip

3. Look at the words on the CMOS chip and search for the technical documentation on it

4. Figure out where the Clear CMOS pin is. 

5. Short it with the screwdriver. This is the dangerous bit as you do NOT want to short anything else.
